original_question: Fix r > 0 and let M \subset \mathbb{R}^2 be a finite set with |M| = n. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Let G_\Sigma be the set of energetic points of \Sigma, where x \in \Sigma is energetic if there exists y \in M such that |xy| = r and B_r(y) \cap \Sigma = \emptyset. How does an explicit description of a minimizer \Sigma depend on M in terms of the degrees of the resulting equations? Under the simplifying assumption that the points of M have rational coordinates, what is the largest degree of the extension of \mathbb{Q} generated by the set of energetic points G_\Sigma?
target_in_paper: Section 7 open problems on maximal distance minimizers, specifically the pair of adjacent problems summarized as full algebraic characterization for finite M (degrees of the defining equations) and reconstruction/characterization via the set of energetic points.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the maximal-distance-minimizer setting, focuses on the finite-target case, and brings in the set G_Σ of energetic points, which is indeed one of the paper’s highlighted structural tools. It also aims at the paper’s algebraic/explicit-description direction rather than at a broader neighboring topic.
missing_details: The paper’s nearest official formulation is not a bound on [Q(G_Σ):Q]; it is an open problem asking for a full algebraic characterization of minimizers for finite M in terms of the degrees of the defining equations.
The paper also separately asks about reconstruction/characterization from the energetic set G_Σ; your draft merges that adjacent problem into the algebraic one.
The rational-coordinate hypothesis is your added arithmetic specialization, not the paper’s stated formulation.
The paper’s wording is about describing the minimizer(s) themselves, not only the field generated by the energetic points.
Your draft fixes the ambient space to ℝ^2, whereas the paper’s open-problem summary does not, in the accessible source, state that planar restriction as part of the official formulation.
It should be explicit whether the question concerns one minimizer or all minimizers for the given data (M,r). The paper’s wording is about the class of minimizers for finite M.
The phrase explicit description should be tied to defining equations and their algebraic degrees, since that is the paper’s actual emphasis.
If G_Σ is included, the paper-faithful formulation should ask whether Σ is characterized or reconstructible from G_Σ, rather than replacing that by a number-theoretic degree question.
refined_question: Let M be a finite subset of Euclidean space and let r > 0. For maximal distance minimizers Σ, that is, connected compact sets of minimal H^1-length subject to M ⊂ B_r(Σ), obtain a full algebraic characterization of the minimizer(s) for finite M: describe Σ by explicit defining equations and determine the algebraic degrees involved; moreover, determine to what extent a minimizer is characterized or can be reconstructed from its set G_Σ of energetic points.
justification: The draft is closest not to a theorem or conjecture elsewhere in the paper, but to the Section 7 maximal-distance-minimizer open problems. The strongest match is the problem about a full algebraic characterization for finite M, because your draft asks how an explicit description of Σ depends on M through equation degrees. Its introduction of G_Σ points directly to the immediately adjacent open problem on reconstruction/characterization from energetic points. However, the paper-faithful formulation does not add the arithmetic specialization to rational coordinates or ask for the maximal degree of the extension generated by G_Σ; that is a stronger number-theoretic variant introduced by the draft, not the official question in the paper. The abstract confirms that the paper is a collection of open questions in maximal distance minimizers and Steiner trees, so the refined version should remain an open-problem-style prompt and stay narrow to those two adjacent Section 7 questions.
